name: IL-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about five points on partisanship
Melissa Bean benefits from roughly $5.5 million in outside support and outraised Jennifer Davis
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot removes Krishnamoorthi's personal advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 94 percent
model.rationale: The seat's Democratic lean, Bean's large fundraising and outside-spending edge, and markets pricing her near 94 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the open seat and absence of any public polling warrant a modest trim from the safest rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Davis closing within single digits, or a shift in the national environment toward Republicans, would move this toward a narrower Lean D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Raja Krishnamoorthi (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats defend an open suburban Chicago seat after Raja Krishnamoorthi left the district to run for Senate. The district leans Democratic by about five points, and Melissa Bean, a former one-term incumbent, enters with a strong financial position: she has raised over $2 million and benefits from roughly $5.5 million in outside support, well ahead of Republican Jennifer Davis's $1.5 million raised.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on partisanship, money, and prediction markets, which price the Democratic side near 94 percent. The open-seat dynamic removes the incumbent's personal edge, but the fundamentals still favor Democrats by a wide margin in this Likely D race.
